summary: Onboarding template desync: duplicate service-account creation and conflicting desk assignment
description:
Issue summary:
HR intake created a new hire (FT-2026-03-09) using the standard onboarding template. Two automated workers then processed the request: the Onboarder job (HR -> PeopleOps) and the Provisioner job (platform-automation). They created overlapping artifacts:

- Two service accounts were auto-created in the platform namespace: platform-sa-maria.1 and platform-sa-maria.2. The duplication caused the CI job that binds team roles to fail intermittently.
- Desk allocation in the facilities system was assigned to two locations (SFO-Desk-122 and SFO-Desk-141) due to a stale mapping between HR template 'preferred_desk' value and facilities sync. Facilities then created a desk reservation for both ids.

Impact:
- Onboarding blocked: engineering onboarding checklist prevented finalizing access because the provisioning audit detected duplicate service accounts.
- CI flakes: new hire could not run initial onboarding pipelines for first-day tasks until manual cleanup.
- Facilities confusion: two desks reserved for same start date causing manager frustration.

Background:
We recently updated the HR onboarding template field names in PeopleOps to consolidate 'workspace_preference' and 'preferred_desk' into a single 'desk_choice' attribute to support hoteling. The platform Provisioner still reads the older 'preferred_desk' key. The Onboarder job was updated at 2026-03-01 but rollout to the automation fleet was staggered; some runners still process an older template.

Steps observed / reproduction notes:
1) HR creates hire record for Maria Lopez on 2026-03-09 using the new consolidated template.
2) Onboarder job (older runner) triggers and creates service account platform-sa-maria.1 and posts a facilities reservation for SFO-Desk-122.
3) Provisioner job (new runner) triggers later and reads the new field, creates platform-sa-maria.2 and posts SFO-Desk-141 reservation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create hire with mixed-field template (include both 'desk_choice' and simulate legacy 'preferred_desk'). 2) Trigger both old and new onboarding runners (or simulate race) 3) Observe duplicate service accounts created in IAM and two desk reservations in facilities.
investigation_notes: Checked PeopleOps template change log: 'desk_choice' introduced 2026-02-28, migration flagged 'preferred_desk' deprecated but still readable.
Provisioner log (2026-03-09T10:14Z): processed payload with 'desk_choice': 'SFO-Desk-141' and created platform-sa-maria.2; no idempotency key present.
Onboarder runner (older image) log (2026-03-09T10:11Z): processed payload with 'preferred_desk': 'SFO-Desk-122' and created platform-sa-maria.1.
IAM audit shows both accounts created within 3 minutes of each other. No automated cleanup job ran because deletion guard requires source to be marked 'reconciled'.
Facilities API: two active reservations exist for same employee start date; facilities UI allowed duplicate reservations from different sync ids.
No existing linked issue about template migration rollout was raised to automation-ops prior to the incident.
comments: Maya Chen (reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed hire couldn't finish onboarding; blocked on access. Please advise whether PeopleOps should revert template or if platform should tolerate both keys.

Evan Brooks (assignee) 2026-03-10: Assigned for triage. Reproduced locally by replaying payloads. Root cause appears to be lack of idempotency and field-name drift between runners. Will propose immediate mitigation.

Priya Kapoor (Infra) 2026-03-11: Suggest adding an idempotency_key tied to hire_id when creating service accounts. Also recommend Facilities add a uniqueness constraint for reservations with overlapping dates.
SRE team lead (Zach Turner) 2026-03-11: Note that provisioning runners are on a staged rollout; ops should pause newer runners until all are upgraded or run-time compatibility shim added.

Maya Chen 2026-03-12: HR would prefer not to revert PeopleOps changes if a compatibility shim can be deployed quickly. HR asks for a documented policy about who owns service-account creation moving forward.
resolution: Pending policy decision. Interim mitigation applied: 1) Rolled back new Provisioner runners for the 2 affected fleet shards to stop duplicate creations. 2) Runbook step added: manual reconciliation script to merge duplicate service accounts and cancel duplicate facilities reservations for the affected hires. 3) Added idempotency_key prototype to platform-sa creation endpoint; still needs PR review and rollout.
follow_up_tasks: Create a formal policy doc: single owner for service-account lifecycle (PeopleOps vs Platform).
Enforce idempotency on service-account creation endpoints (deploy PR 812 to canary after review).
Add uniqueness constraint to Facilities reservation service for same-employee/start-date.
Run a one-week audit of onboarded hires to detect any other duplicates and reconcile.
Schedule a cross-team postmortem discussion: PeopleOps, Provisioner, Onboarder, Facilities, and SRE.
